Satisfaction, Shorts & the 2026 Rulebook

6 min read · Updated November 2026 · Free · Written for Kenya
Share: WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram LinkedIn

Shorts can now be up to 3 minutes long, but if a Short over 1 minute gets any copyright claim, YouTube blocks it worldwide. Under 1 minute, the same claim doesn't block it.

Since 15 October 2024, square or vertical videos up to three minutes upload as Shorts. The catch is in YouTube's help page: Shorts longer than one minute with an active Content ID claim "are blocked globally". They can't be watched, recommended or monetised until the claim is resolved. That one song from the radio can kill a 90-second Short.

Your ShortCopyright claim?Result
Under 1 minuteYesNot blocked by this rule (normal claim terms apply)
1–3 minutesYes, any typeBlocked globally until the claim is resolved
1–3 minutesMusic from YouTube Audio LibraryRoyalty-free library music won't trigger Content ID

Satisfaction: the scoreboard you can't see

Beaupré: "No metric on its own is a good indicator of value." YouTube mixes watch time with likes, dislikes, shares and viewer surveys to estimate whether people were glad they watched. A tight 5-minute video that answers the question beats a 12-minute one padded to look long.

✗ MYTH

Longer videos always win because they collect more watch time.

✓ REALITY

Watch time still matters, but YouTube is also asking whether the viewer felt the time was well spent. Padding to hit a length usually shows up as a dip in retention and weaker survey answers.

Three 2026 facts most Kenyan creators haven't heard

  • Hype isn't here yet. The Hype button lets fans push videos from channels with 500–500,000 subscribers up a leaderboard. When it rolled out to 39 countries in August 2025, Africa wasn't included. Check your Studio before planning around it.
  • The Shorts view count changed. Public views count every play since March 2025; engaged views (people who chose to keep watching) are what YouTube uses for YPP and earnings.
  • "Unsatisfying" is now a monetisation category. Content that "relies heavily on emotionally manipulative formulas" can lose ad eligibility, even if it gets views.
💡 What most creators miss

Your rewatch spikes are free ideas. In the retention graph, a bump upward means people dragged back to watch a moment again. That moment, under 60 seconds and with your own or library audio, is your next Short.

✅ Do this today
⚡ Quick check

Your 2-minute Short uses a popular song and gets a Content ID claim. What happens?

YouTube's help page says Shorts over one minute with an active claim of any type are blocked globally. Under a minute, this rule doesn't apply.

🧠 Key takeaways
  1. Shorts can be 3 minutes, but over 1 minute any copyright claim blocks them worldwide.
  2. YouTube weighs satisfaction (likes, dislikes, surveys), not just minutes watched.
  3. Hype hasn't reached Africa; engaged views, not the public counter, decide Shorts money.
